insight_title: DUR public comment is in-person only, capped, and constrained to one speaker per manufacturer
why_it_matters: Manufacturers cannot rely on virtual attendance or multiple aligned speakers; the practical window opens only after agenda posting and closes 24 hours before the meeting.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Speaker registration forms must be received after agenda posting and no later than 24 hours before the meeting; public comment is capped at 40 total minutes, each speaker gets 5 minutes if eight or fewer speakers register, only one speaker per manufacturer is allowed, and public comment through Zoom is not allowed.
validation_note: Verified in agenda text lines 81-97; page marker shows Page 2.

insight_title: Migraine CGRP step burden explicitly changes if supplemental rebates lapse
why_it_matters: The access barrier is not just clinical; rebate participation is directly tied to whether preferred CGRP products require two or three prior preventive therapy failures.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The packet states that Ajovy and Emgality manufacturers provided supplemental rebates to be preferred CGRP inhibitors and require trials with two other migraine preventive therapies; if they do not participate in supplemental rebates, they revert to original criteria requiring trials with three other therapies.
validation_note: Verified in packet text lines 8791-8800; page marker shows Page 211.

insight_title: HAE PBPA tiers put new Andembry, Dawnzera, and Ekterly behind lower-tier failures despite first-in-class positioning
drug_or_class: Andembry, Dawnzera, Ekterly, HAE prophylaxis and treatment products
why_it_matters: Launch messaging around oral administration or novel mechanisms may not overcome Oklahoma's proposed PBPA tier structure without patient-specific reasons why lower-tier HAE products cannot be used.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The College recommended Special PA placement for Andembry and Dawnzera in HAE prophylaxis and for Ekterly in HAE treatment, with Special PA criteria requiring a clinically significant reason why the member cannot use all other lower-tiered HAE products. The packet also quantifies a $175,984.39 per member-year spread between highest and lowest prophylaxis options and a $13,632.87 per treatment-dose spread between highest and lowest acute products.
validation_note: Verified in packet text lines 6808-6829 and 6835-6953; page markers show Pages 119-121.

insight_title: Line-extension muscle relaxants show extreme unit-cost scrutiny before PA votes
drug_or_class: Tanlor, metaxalone 640 mg, Zanaflex 8 mg, methocarbamol and tizanidine formulations
why_it_matters: Formulation and strength launches can trigger PA even where older generics share the indication and dose logic; dossiers should anticipate formulation-substitution and cost-per-day comparisons.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The February 2026 packet compares Tanlor 1,000 mg at $2,820 per 30 days with methocarbamol 500 mg at $7.20 and 750 mg at $6.00, and compares metaxalone 640 mg at $7,500 per 30 days with metaxalone 800 mg at $60.00; costs are based on NADAC, WAC, or SMAC and do not reflect rebates or net costs.
validation_note: Verified in packet text lines 7104-7131 and 7170-7193; page markers show Pages 127-128.

insight_title: MASH criteria make Rezdiffra step through semaglutide, with pioglitazone added for type 2 diabetes
why_it_matters: The MASH access path favors older or broader metabolic therapies before a branded MASH-specific agent, and renewal requires histologic or noninvasive evidence of response.
evidence_quote_or_summary: For Rezdiffra, concurrent type 2 diabetes requires failure of a 6-month trial of semaglutide combined with pioglitazone; without type 2 diabetes, failure of a 6-month semaglutide trial is required. Renewal requires resolution of steatohepatitis without worsening fibrosis, fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening steatohepatitis, or both.
validation_note: Verified in handout text lines 1440-1496; page marker shows Page 24.

insight_title: Zepbound OSA coverage excludes diabetes and requires CPAP plus weight-management failure
why_it_matters: Even with an OSA indication, coverage is narrowed to non-diabetic patients after documented specialist involvement, PSG-defined disease, six months of comprehensive weight management, and six months of CPAP failure.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Initial OSA criteria require specialist prescribing/consult, moderate to severe OSA with AHI >15 by attended sleep study or PSG, no type 2 diabetes, BMI at least 30 with a comorbidity, six months of comprehensive weight management including pharmacotherapy, and failed six-month CPAP trial. Renewal requires at least 20% AHI decrease, remission/mild non-symptomatic OSA, or at least 10% weight loss.
validation_note: Verified in handout text lines 1377-1415; page markers show Pages 22-23.

insight_title: Primary biliary cholangitis agents require biopsy, ursodiol failure, alcohol testing, and lab-defined renewal
why_it_matters: Evidence strategy needs to address diagnostic confirmation and objective biochemical response, not only FDA label alignment or symptom burden.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Initial criteria for non-preferred Iqirvo, Livdelzi, and Ocaliva require FDA-label use, hepatologist or gastroenterologist prescribing/consult, liver-biopsy confirmation, no terminal diagnosis, no decompensated cirrhosis, at least six months of ursodiol failure with ALP >1.67x ULN or bilirubin >ULN, and alcohol testing if alcohol use occurred within five years. Renewal requires ALP/bilirubin response or, for Livdelzi, itch benefit after failed cholestyramine, rifampin, and naltrexone.
validation_note: Verified in handout text lines 2695-2735; page markers show Pages 39-40.

insight_title: Non-solid dosage forms face point-of-sale age edits even when no clinical PA applies
why_it_matters: Liquid, oral film, sprinkle, or other non-solid formulations may reject for members aged 10 or older even outside class-specific PA, creating a formulation-specific barrier for products positioned around administration convenience.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Non-solid dosage forms that do not require prior authorization for clinical criteria reject at point of sale for members 10 years and older to verify non-solid dosage-form criteria; approval requires a feeding tube need, swallow-study documentation, permanent disability swallowing solids, or a short-term restriction such as mouth surgery.
validation_note: Verified in handout text lines 14109-14135; page marker shows Page 223.

insight_title: PDL recommendations are not final until DHHS Secretary approval, with a 30-day comment cycle
why_it_matters: Monitoring should not stop at Review Panel votes; there is a formal Secretary approval step and a quarterly cadence that can affect implementation timing.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The October 2025 minutes state that the 2023 law established quarterly PDL Review Panel meetings, a public comment period, and a procedure for Review Panel recommendations to the Secretary of DHHS; the public comment period is 30 days, and recommendations approved by the panel are submitted to the DHHS Secretary for final approval.
validation_note: Verified in minutes text lines 50-64; page marker shows Page 1.

insight_title: Wegovy was preferred only for MACE risk reduction and still required manual PA
why_it_matters: A preferred PDL position did not equal broad obesity access; coverage was restricted to the cardiovascular risk-reduction indication and explicitly did not auto-approve.
evidence_quote_or_summary: July 2024 minutes added Wegovy as preferred only for cardiovascular risk reduction. Discussion notes say that even though preferred, PA is required and will not have auto-approved PAs; coverage is only for reducing major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease who are obese or overweight, while full coverage of weight-loss agents was pending.
validation_note: Verified in minutes text lines 578-597; page markers show Pages 8-9.

insight_title: GLP-1 weight-management coverage was reinstated off-cycle but still split preferred versus non-preferred access
why_it_matters: Coverage shifts can occur outside scheduled reviews, but Zepbound and Saxenda remained non-preferred products requiring trial-and-failure and clinical criteria.
evidence_quote_or_summary: January 2026 minutes state that, under the Governor's directive, NC Medicaid coverage for GLP-1s for obesity was reinstated effective Dec. 12, 2025, reverting to criteria in place as of Sept. 30, 2025. Wegovy was added back as preferred, while Zepbound and Saxenda were added back as non-preferred and were to be reviewed at the April PDL panel meeting.
validation_note: Verified in minutes text lines 78-89; page marker shows Page 2.

insight_title: Outside parties can request an Oregon ad hoc expert 21 days before review, and that expert can vote on confidential-pricing matters
drug_or_class: P&T Committee ad hoc subject matter experts
why_it_matters: For niche therapies, expert selection is an underused leverage point: a qualified Oregon expert can receive voting rights on utilization controls and confidential pricing for the affected PDL drugs.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Oregon operating procedures allow an interested outside party to request appointment of an ad hoc expert at least 21 calendar days before the P&T meeting if the committee lacks clinical knowledge. Appointed experts must be licensed and actively practicing in Oregon and have full voting rights on the PDL drugs for which they were selected, including utilization controls, PA requirements, review of confidential pricing information, and other PDL conditions.
validation_note: Verified in operating procedures text lines 47-64; page marker context is Page 2.

insight_title: Oregon values comparative new evidence over label recitation, with two-week lead time for clinical written testimony
why_it_matters: Manufacturer testimony that repeats prescribing information is explicitly deprioritized; useful submissions need comparative evidence and enough lead time for staff review.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Oral testimony sign-up and conflict forms are requested no later than 24 hours before the meeting; speakers get three minutes per speaker/institution per agenda item. The most helpful information is evidence-based comparative research limited to new information, while oral presentation of FDA-approved labeling is 'not helpful.' Clinical written testimony should be submitted at least two weeks before the meeting, and written documents during testimony are limited to two pages of new information.
validation_note: Verified in operating procedures text lines 128-166; page marker shows Page 4.

insight_title: New drugs can be held to interim PA for non-funded indications or $5,000 claim/month cost before P&T review
drug_or_class: New drugs, line extensions, combination products, biosimilars
why_it_matters: Oregon has explicit pre-review controls that can affect launch uptake before a formal P&T vote, especially for high-cost products and non-funded conditions.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Until P&T review, new drugs may be reviewed for FDA-approved or compendia-supported indication, FDA-approved dosing, and OHP-funded indication if they are in a class with clinical PA, used for a non-funded HERC condition, or cost more than $5,000 per claim or per month. New significant line extensions are not preferred until reviewed, and combination products and biosimilars are designated non-preferred until reviewed.
validation_note: Verified in operating procedures text lines 188-228; page markers show Pages 5-6.

insight_title: Industry must use the Single PDL mailbox and avoid direct committee contact on PDL status
why_it_matters: The state creates a controlled submission route and bars direct member lobbying, so relationship-driven outreach to committee members can backfire or be disregarded.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The South Carolina P&T page requests pharmaceutical industry members submit information regarding potential PDL drugs to SCSinglePDL@primetherapeutics.com and not directly contact or mail P&T Committee members or staff about PDL status. Committee members must not discuss PDL status issues with industry.
validation_note: Verified in extracted HTML text around the P&T Committee Policies section; HTML source has no page numbers.

insight_title: Non-preferred wakefulness drugs require only one preferred failure, while Uzedy gets a pediatric PA carveout
why_it_matters: South Carolina exposes different access levers in one meeting: a relatively shallow one-preferred-agent step for anti-narcolepsy agents and an age-based PA trigger for a long-acting antipsychotic.
evidence_quote_or_summary: August 2025 minutes add armodafinil and modafinil generics as preferred and Nuvigil, Provigil, Sunosi, and Wakix as non-preferred, with all non-preferred medications requiring trial and failure of one preferred agent plus clinical criteria. The same minutes add Uzedy as preferred but require prior authorizations for children less than or equal to 6 years of age; the class changes were effective Jan. 1, 2026.
validation_note: Verified in August 2025 minutes text lines 128-135, 155-168, and 176-179; page markers show Pages 3-4.

insight_title: Clinical submissions must distinguish products within class and late/off-topic/hard-copy material is ignored
why_it_matters: Rhode Island narrows manufacturer evidence to differentiating clinical information for products under review and enforces a specific pre-meeting deadline.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The P&T page says clinical information relevant to products being reviewed must be submitted to Karen Mariano and should be limited to information that distinguishes the product from others in its therapeutic class. For the June 2, 2026 meeting, the deadline was Tuesday, May 19, 2026; late documents, hard-copy documents, or documents for medications not under review will not be reviewed by the committee.
validation_note: Verified in extracted HTML around 'Submission of Clinical Information'; HTML source has no page numbers.

insight_title: Bylaws bar advance manufacturer clinical packets and cap meeting materials to one-page bullets
why_it_matters: The public meeting is not a broad dossier channel; manufacturers have four minutes total and cannot rely on package inserts or advance clinical packet submissions.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Rhode Island bylaws allow one speaking opportunity per company/manufacturer/group, with four minutes total even with multiple speakers. Materials are restricted to one 8.5 x 11 single-sided page of bulleted information, no audiovisual equipment can be used, and no clinical submissions by manufacturers or organizations, including package inserts, are accepted in advance for committee packets or distributed during the meeting.
validation_note: Verified in bylaws text lines 117-136; page marker shows Page 4.

insight_title: Manufacturer presentations are clinical-only, Friday-confirmed, and written materials are due two business days before vote
why_it_matters: Ohio permits manufacturer presentation, but the format excludes price discussion and imposes short, specific timing gates before committee votes.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Ohio bylaws say manufacturers whose products are under review may present or submit written material but should focus on relative clinical merits and not discuss price or committee business with members outside the public meeting. Requests to present must be received by 5:00 pm on the Friday before the meeting, presentations are limited to three minutes, and written materials should be submitted electronically at least two business days before the meeting.
validation_note: Verified in bylaws text lines 146-205; page marker shows Page 4.

insight_title: Medicaid Director must act within 30 days and publicly explain rejected P&T recommendations
why_it_matters: Committee action is advisory, but Ohio has a defined post-recommendation clock and transparency obligation when the Director rejects a recommendation.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Ohio law states that the Director shall act on the committee's recommendations no later than 30 days after the recommendation is posted; if the Director does not accept a recommendation, the Director must present the basis within 14 days after the determination or at the next scheduled meeting, whichever is sooner.
validation_note: Verified in statute PDF text lines 49-56; extracted text around this section is on Page 2.

insight_title: Wegovy non-obesity criteria exclude diabetes and require cardiovascular standard-of-care plus 5% renewal weight loss
drug_or_class: Wegovy and GLP-1 receptor agonists for non-obesity indications
why_it_matters: Ohio's non-obesity GLP-1 path turns MACE coverage into a tightly documented cardiovascular-risk pathway and keeps diabetes patients in a different category.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Draft April 2026 minutes list 180-day authorizations for GLP-1 agonists for non-obesity indications. MACE criteria require age 18 or older, BMI at least 27, no combination with another GLP-1/GLP-1-GIP, documentation of prior MI/stroke/symptomatic PAD, standard cardiovascular care, and no type 1 or type 2 diabetes for Wegovy. Subsequent MACE authorization requires efficacy/safety monitoring, chart-noted weight loss of at least 5%, and 80% PDC by claims.
validation_note: Verified in draft minutes text lines 1570-1655; page markers show Pages 21-22.

insight_title: Public testimony requires 14-day registration, one manufacturer per product, two minutes, and no Q&A
why_it_matters: Pennsylvania testimony slots are scarce and procedurally constrained; first registration can determine which manufacturer representative is heard for a product.
evidence_quote_or_summary: P&T bylaws require testimony registration at least 14 days before the meeting, first-come first-served. Only one manufacturer representative may testify per product; if more than one registers, the first is allowed and others are declined. Spoken testimony is two minutes, written materials are limited to one single-sided page of bullets, and there is no question-and-answer period.
validation_note: Verified in bylaws text lines 138-158; page marker shows Page 4.

insight_title: Journavx acute-pain PA is limited to 14 days and resets only for distinct new pain episodes
why_it_matters: Vertex or competitors should frame access around short-course acute pain episodes, prior acetaminophen/NSAID failure, and documentation of distinct repeat episodes rather than ongoing pain use.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The Jan. 5, 2026 bulletin adds Analgesics, Acute Pain Agents to the Statewide PDL and applies guidelines in FFS and managed care. Criteria require therapeutic failure/contraindication/intolerance to acetaminophen and an NSAID. For Journavx, the beneficiary must not have received a 14-day supply in the past 90 days, or documentation must show a new moderate-to-severe acute pain episode distinct from the prior Journavx-treated episode. Requests are approved for up to 14 days; physician reviewer judgment can override when medically necessary.
validation_note: Verified in bulletin text lines 24-35 and 145-206; page markers show Page 5 for the criteria.

insight_title: DURB recommendations move from public comment to clinical review to cost review before Commissioner selection
why_it_matters: NYRx preferred status is not purely a public clinical vote; cost information enters after public comment and clinical research, and the Commissioner is the final selection point.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The PDP page says DURB reviews drug classes and makes recommendations to the Commissioner of Health on preferred and non-preferred drugs and clinical criteria for non-preferred PA. Recommendations are based on public comment and testimony, objective clinical research, then drug cost information. Upcoming board activities are posted 30 days prior to meetings.
validation_note: Verified in extracted HTML around the Commissioner and DURB description; HTML source has no page numbers.

insight_title: Some CDRP drugs require prescriber-only PA initiation and clinical-call-center evidence
why_it_matters: Products assigned to CDRP can face workflow barriers beyond standard ePA, including prescriber-only initiation and faxed clinical support.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The CDRP page states certain drugs require PA because of safety issues, public health concerns, fraud/abuse potential, or significant overuse/misuse. For some CDRP drugs, only prescribers, not authorized agents, can initiate PA. Each CDRP drug has specific clinical information that must be provided to the clinical call center, and prescribers may be asked to fax it.
validation_note: Verified in extracted HTML around 'Clinical Drug Review Program (CDRP) About'; HTML source has no page numbers.
